main.description: Where a seller ships and how soon they dispatch. Its own record rather than fields on the shop: shipping coverage changes with carrier contracts and seasons while a shop's name and logo do not, and putting the first two fields of a fulfillment system inside seller identity would oblige every later field — pickup locations, per-class handling, regional cutoffs — to follow them there. This record says where and how soon, never how much: rate tables, rate calculation, carrier selection, and label generation are out of scope and belong to a fulfillment system. A profile applies to the whole shop; when per-class coverage is needed, an appliesTo selector belongs on this record rather than a pointer on every listing.

subject.description: AT URI of the shop this profile belongs to

title.description: Display name, e.g. 'EU express'. Several profiles per shop is the point of a tid key — a seller may reach the EU in two days and the rest of the world in ten — so they need distinguishing.

handlingTime.description: Working days between an order and its dispatch. A dispatch promise, not a delivery estimate: time in transit depends on carrier and destination, which this schema does not model.

coverage.description: Which destinations the seller serves. Destinations only — methods, rates, and routing are a fulfillment system's concern.

worldwide.description: True if the seller ships anywhere, subject to excludedCountries

countries.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes the seller ships to. Redundant when worldwide is true.

excludedCountries.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes the seller will not ship to, subtracted from worldwide or from countries.
